translations.answer: No. AMASS uses MoSh++ to convert heterogeneous motion-capture data into a common SMPL-H+DMPL surface representation, making it useful upstream material for motion retargeting. Before it enters Whole-Body Control (WBC) training, each result still requires joint-limit, self-collision, foot-contact, dynamic-trackability, and license checks.
translations.applicability.assumptions.0: The licenses of every upstream motion dataset, the SMPL model, and exported data have been reviewed.
translations.applicability.assumptions.1: Robot references pass a separate retargeting, contact-repair, and closed-loop tracking acceptance process.
translations.applicability.environments.0: Offline preparation of human motion data.
translations.applicability.robots.0: Target humanoid unspecified; applies to robots that consume human-motion references.
translations.confidence_rationale: The unified representation, scale, and held-out scan errors are supported by the paper. Confidence is bounded because no target robot's dynamic feasibility was evaluated.
translations.evidence.0.locator: Figures 1, 3, and 6–9; Table 1; Sections 3–5; and the appendix.
translations.evidence.0.note: Defines the two-stage MoSh++ fit, unified SMPL-H+DMPL representation, scan errors, and dataset scale.
translations.evidence.0.title: AMASS: Archive of Motion Capture as Surface Shapes
translations.title: Can unified human motion from AMASS be used directly as a humanoid training reference?
